fixes.title: Shell equipment indicator reads "0/0 - No devices configured" while four devices are connected
fixes.summary: _countConnectedDevices required `profileDeviceId != null`, so a connection made through the app's own "This session only - not saved to your profile" flow could never be counted, and the guard at the top of the popup body (`!hasAnyDevice && connectedCount == 0`) then replaced every per-device row with the literal 'No devices configured'. Replaced both counters with one _countDevices pass producing a _EquipmentCounts value that keeps THREE numbers: assignedConnected / assignedTotal (the profile ratio, still profile-scoped so the old '4/2 reads as a broken counter' regression documented in the removed comment cannot come back - that constraint is why the naive 'just count everything' fix is wrong) and sessionOnlyConnected, reported explicitly. The chip now reads '4 connected' when the profile assigns nothing, '2/2 +1' when something is attached outside the profile, and plain '1/2' otherwise; the tooltip spells the same facts out in words; the status dot is derived from the same value so a session-only rig is no longer painted muted-grey as if nothing were attached; and 'No devices configured' now requires that nothing be assigned AND nothing be attached.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the session-only arm of the tally closure in _countDevices - `} else if (isConnected) { sessionOnlyConnected++; }` became `}` (equipment_status_indicator.dart:110), which is exactly the old profile-scoped rule. 2 of 4 tests FAILED: 'counts session-only connections the profile does not assign' (Found 0 widgets with text "4 connected") and 'keeps the profile ratio and reports extras separately' (Found 0 widgets with text "2/2 +1"). Restored -> 4 passed. The sever cuts production wiring, not a helper: the tests pump the real EquipmentStatusIndicator inside a ProviderScope with the real CameraStateNotifier/MountStateNotifier/FocuserStateNotifier/FilterWheelStateNotifier driven through setConnecting+setConnected, tap the real chip, and read the rendered popup.
fixes.caveats: The finding also asked for a per-device Disconnect in the popup. Not done - that is a new control, not a false statement; the popup keeps its existing Disconnect All. Device rows are still built from the six imaging slots only, so a connected weather/safety/dome/switch device is still neither counted nor listed (it never was, and is not part of this claim - but it is the same shape of omission).

fixes.title: Slew dropdown drives the mount 69 degrees BELOW the horizon and reports 'Slew complete'
fixes.summary: Added a horizon precondition to the shared slew control, in _handleSlewMode so it covers ALL THREE menu entries (Slew, Slew & Center, Slew Center & Rotate) rather than only the plain slew - the verifier correctly noted _preflightCentering checks the camera and the solver but never the sky, so fixing only _handleSlew would have left the centering paths open. _confirmHorizon computes the target's alt/az with SchedulerService.calculateAltAz - the same model the scheduler uses to decide what is worth imaging, so the slew gate and the planner cannot disagree about where a target is - and compares it against the site's effective horizon (Settings > Location, default 0 deg = the mathematical horizon). Below the ground it raises a destructive 'Target is below the horizon' confirm naming the depth and the azimuth and warning about the pier/tripod strike; between 0 deg and the configured floor it raises a softer 'below your horizon limit' confirm. Both are confirmations, not blocks: a below-horizon GoTo is occasionally deliberate and a hard refusal would strand those users. The gate runs BEFORE _operationInFlight latches, so a refused slew leaves the button unchanged. Settings are AWAITED (appSettingsProvider.future), not read cold - a cold read returns AsyncLoading on first touch and would have made the gate silently pass, which is the dangerous direction; this is the same pattern and the same reason as the centering dialog's _resolvedAppSettings. With no observing site on record the command goes through unchallenged rather than being judged against an invented horizon, and 'is there a site' stays appObserverLocationProvider's call so (0,0) is not re-litigated here.
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/widgets/slew_dropdown_button_test.dart  (8 passed, 5 new)
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the two-line call site from _handleSlewMode - `if (!await _confirmHorizon()) return;` plus its `if (!_isCurrentOperation(revision, backend)) return;` (slew_dropdown_button.dart:194-195), leaving _confirmHorizon defined but unreached. 4 of 8 FAILED: 'a below-horizon target is not dispatched without a confirm', 'confirming the horizon warning sends the slew', 'the configured horizon floor is enforced above 0 degrees' and 'Slew & Center is gated too' (all: Found 0 widgets with text "Target is below the horizon"). Restored -> 8 passed. The sever cuts the production WIRING (the call site inside the real onSelected handler), not the helper: the tests pump the real SlewDropdownButton via pumpAppScreen, open the real PopupMenuButton, tap the real menu entries, and assert on MountCommandService.slewTo call counts. Declinations were chosen so the verdict does not depend on the wall clock - from lat +45, Dec -80 can never rise above -35 deg and Dec +85 is circumpolar between +40 and +50 - so there is no mocked clock to drift.
fixes.caveats: The gate is on the shared widget, which is the surface the finding reproduced on (Imaging > Mount > GoTo/Sync) and also covers Framing. It does NOT cover the five GoTo entry points that call MountCommandService.slewTo directly: planetarium_screen.dart:242, planetarium_screen/actions.dart:334/348/378/473, planetarium/widgets/info_tab.dart:97 and first_light/widgets/transient_candidate_card.dart:369. Those still slew below the horizon silently. See needs_shared_change - the durable fix is the same precondition inside MountCommandService.slewTo, after which this widget gate becomes the (still useful) UI affordance rather than the only guard.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/services/mount_command_service.dart - slewTo currently validates coordinate RANGE only (mount_command_service.dart:179-206) and then unconditionally returns success('Slew complete'). Move the altitude precondition there (compute alt/az from appObserverLocationProvider + SchedulerService.calculateAltAz, refuse or require an explicit override flag below the effective horizon) so the planetarium, the transient card and any future caller inherit it. The widget's _confirmHorizon can then become the UI that supplies that override.

fixes.title: Connection troubleshooter says it 'couldn't pin down the exact cause' while holding an error that names the exact cause, then gives four irrelevant hardware steps
fixes.summary: Confirmed real, and the verifier's location correction is right: packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/troubleshooter/connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart is a pure renderer - it calls diagnoseConnectionFailure in initState and paints whatever comes back. Every part of the defect is in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart, which is OUTSIDE my ownership (packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/**), so I did not edit it. I traced the classification by hand against the source: the built-in guider preflight emits five first-party configuration errors from native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/builtin_guider.rs (:1265 'requires a connected camera in the active profile', :1276 '...connected mount...', :1306 'requires an active profile with a guide focal length', :1320 'requires positive camera pixel dimensions', :1329 'requires positive guide focal length and camera pixel size (focal_length_mm=0, ...)'). None of them matches _permissionMarkers, _driverMarkers, _enumerationMarkers or _configurationMarkers; the wrapper text 'Failed to connect built-in guider' DOES match the _networkMarkers entry 'failed to connect' but _classify only consults that list for alpaca/indi, so every one of the five falls through to DiagnosticCategory.unknown - hence the 'we couldn't pin down the exact cause' sentence at :417 and the _unknownSteps playbook at :736-769 that tells the operator to reseat a cable and confirm power on a software guider that has neither. Anything I could have done inside the dialog would have been a SECOND knowledge base sitting on top of the wrong one, i.e. relocation, so I did nothing rather than that.
fixes.test: None written - writing a test for a fix I am not permitted to apply would leave a failing test in the suite. The existing core suite packages/skotiq_core/test/models/connection_diagnostic_test.dart is where the new cases belong.
fixes.caveats: This is a confirmed, unfixed P2. It is not a false positive.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/troubleshooter/connection_diagnostic.dart. (1) Add the built-in-guider preflight strings to _configurationMarkers (:263-274) - the discriminating substrings are 'guide focal length', 'pixel size', 'positive camera pixel dimensions', 'requires an active profile' and 'requires a connected camera/mount in the active profile' - so they classify as DiagnosticCategory.configuration instead of unknown. (2) _configurationSteps (:686-734) currently branches only on ascom / alpaca+indi; give the native/simulator branch a step that names the actual remedy ('Open Equipment > Edit Profile and set the guide scope focal length in mm') rather than the generic 'confirm the correct device is selected'. (3) _unknownSteps (:736-769) should not emit 'Check the <device> is connected and powered / Reseat the cable, confirm power' for a device with no cable and no power - gate that first step on a physical device (driverType native/ascom AND a real hardware DeviceType), because sending a user to reseat a cable that does not exist is worse than silence. A UI affordance to jump to the profile editor would then be a small addition to connection_troubleshooter_dialog.dart, which I do own, but it is pointless until the classifier stops answering 'unknown'.

fixes.title: First Light dialog accepts a 999999-second exposure and has no upper bound, contradicting its own copy
fixes.summary: The guided first-light intro panel is the ONLY producer of the exposure the orchestrator runs, and nothing bounded it above zero: _parseExposure rejected only `value == null || value <= 0`, so 999999 was dispatched verbatim as an 11.6-day exposure the flow has no cancel path for. _parseExposure now returns a ({double? seconds, String? error}) record and refuses anything over a named 120 s ceiling with copy that states the limit and points at the Imaging screen (which has a stop button); the panel's own helper line now names the same 120 s so the promise and the enforcement are the same number. Refusal, not a silent clamp - rewriting the number under the user's cursor would be its own small lie.
fixes.test: cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test test/widgets/first_light/first_light_flow_dialog_test.dart  (13 passed, 2 new)
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the whole upper-bound branch from _parseExposure - the `if (value > _maxExposureSeconds) { return (seconds: null, error: 'First light is capped at ...'); }` block. 'intro panel refuses an exposure past the first-light cap' FAILED (controller.lastRunExposure was 999999.0 and the 'capped at 120 seconds' text was absent). Restored -> 13 passed. The sever cuts the production wiring: the test drives the real dialog through FirstLightFlowDialog.show, types into the real TextField, taps the real Start capture button, and asserts on what the real FirstLightController was asked to run - it also checks 120 itself is still accepted so the cap is a limit and not an off-by-one refusal.
fixes.caveats: The bound is enforced at the only UI that produces it. FirstLightOrchestrator.run still accepts any positive exposure, so a future non-UI caller could reintroduce this; see needs_shared_change.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/first_light/first_light_orchestrator.dart:233-240 - FirstLightOrchestrator.run rejects only `exposureSeconds <= 0`. It should reject (or clamp) above the guided-flow ceiling too, so the invariant does not depend on a widget.

fixes.title: The NIGHT STORY timeline (and every narrator detail sheet) is hidden whenever the session has no science products, even when narrator events exist
fixes.summary: Confirmed real by reading the current source, and the verifier's line-drift correction is right. The defect is in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_tab.dart, which is OUTSIDE my ownership (packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/**) and inside the r-analytics agent's area, so I did not edit it. Current tree: the allEmpty predicate at :472-482 tests ten SCIENCE product collections (lightCurve, transparency, transparencyRows, calibrations, psfTiles, residuals, moving, lineRatios, frameMetrics, tileMetrics) and never looks at the narrator feed; its early-return branch at :488-536 renders the session bar, ScienceStatusBanner, ScienceSolveRateCard, ScienceLadderCard and ScienceEmptyOnramp and then returns - so the NIGHT STORY heading plus NightStoryTimeline(sessionId: activeSessionId) at :687-693 is unreachable, and with it every narrator detail sheet (widgets/narrator/narrator_detail_sheet.dart, which I do own and which is correct - it is simply never reached). NightStoryTimeline already handles the genuinely-empty case itself (night_story_timeline.dart:259-264 and :294-299 render an empty state rather than nothing), so it is safe to render unconditionally in that branch.
fixes.test: None written - the failing widget test belongs next to the file being changed (packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/), and leaving a red test for a fix I am not permitted to apply would be worse than none.
fixes.caveats: This is a confirmed, unfixed P2. narrator_detail_sheet.dart itself (the nominal unit) is not defective.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/science_analytics_tab.dart - render the NIGHT STORY section inside the `if (allEmpty)` branch (:488-536), between ScienceSolveRateCard and ScienceLadderCard, as `_SectionHeading(colors: colors, label: 'NIGHT STORY', icon: LucideIcons.bookOpen)` + `NightStoryTimeline(sessionId: activeSessionId)`. Rendering it unconditionally is preferable to widening the allEmpty predicate with narratorFeedProvider, because the narrator is a session-narrative surface and not a science product - the user this feature was written for (imaged all night, no plate solver) is exactly the user allEmpty is true for. A test should seed imaging_sessions + captured_images + narrator_events with all science tables empty and assert the NIGHT STORY heading renders.
